title: Stage-Adaptive Proteostasis-Immune-Repair Platform
research_questions: Can biomarker-defined state predict response to proteostasis and immune-state interventions?
Does treatment order determine durable disease modification?
Can controlled neural repair restore function after pathological-state normalization?
Which claims generalize between AD and PD and which remain disease-specific?

cure_definition.functional_control: slowed or arrested progression on prespecified functional and circuit endpoints
cure_definition.biological_remission: pathology and maladaptive immune state remain improved through washout without rebound
cure_definition.repair: durable circuit recovery with safe integration after pathology control
cure_definition.release_rule: all applicable levels, safety, and independent replication required for cure label

hypotheses.claim: Proteostasis intervention improves aggregate clearance and neuronal resilience only with validated target engagement.
State-selective immune normalization outperforms broad suppression for neuronal survival and function while preserving protective clearance.
Proteostasis-first or pathology-plus-immune-first sequences outperform repair-first or simultaneous sequences in durable graft survival and circuit rescue.
A composite biomarker state predicts held-out response better than any single biomarker.
Durable remission requires low washout rebound in pathology and function, not transient end-of-treatment improvement.
A shared systems backbone can generalize across AD and PD while protein and circuit modules remain disease-specific.

cellular.models: patient-derived and isogenic iPSC neurons, astrocytes, and microglia
cellular.donor_target: at least 3 independent backgrounds per disease module

analysis.animal: stage-by-sequence longitudinal mixed effects with cage/litter random effects
analysis.prediction: grouped cross-validation by donor, animal, participant, and batch

decision_rules: promote only with target engagement, pathology/function benefit, acceptable safety, washout durability, and independent replication
restrict stage-limited effects to studied stage
do not force a shared AD/PD sequence if cross-disease validation fails
human_review_requirements: clinical protocol and regulatory review before intervention
